§4.5 session-ride key-type chain (framework-level): (1) SSO form posts string-named inputs including Rails-nested `utm_data[<key>]` (GoogleSSOButton.tsx diff, name={"utm_data[" + key + "]"}); (2) rack-2.2.9 Request#params merges GET/POST parsed via `parse_nested_query` (rack/request.rb:31,440–468,589–590) → `{'utm_data' => {'<key>' => '<val>'}}`, string keys, Hash responds to empty? as §4.5 claims; (3) setup lambda (omniauth-2.0.4 strategy.rb:356–365 runs options[:setup] on BOTH request_call:234 and callback_call:266) writes `env['rack.session'][:oauth_tracking]` — ActionDispatch::Request::Session#[]= (actionpack-6.1.7.7 request/session.rb:131–134) stringifies the key to 'oauth_tracking'; inner keys already strings from %w[]; (4) on the callback request Google's redirect params (state/code) match no allowed key, so the pre-existing `.any?` guard skips the write and the ridden value survives; (5) cookie round-trip uses the :json serializer (config/initializers/cookies_serializer.rb:7 confirmed at HEAD) — all keys, including inner utm_data keys, come back as strings; (6) controller `session.delete(:oauth_tracking)` (Request::Session#delete, session.rb:165–168, stringifies to 'oauth_tracking') matches the write, and `request.env['omniauth.params']` is the string-keyed `request.GET` hash stored at strategy.rb:238 and restored at :270 — so the §4.7 string-key reads are correct on both the cross-request and same-request paths.

One non-finding observation for completeness: sanitizeTrackingValue drops ANY trailing high surrogate, including one an input value could theoretically arrive with pre-truncation — unreachable in practice because window.location.search is a USVString (browsers replace lone surrogates with U+FFFD) and decode-uri-component's malformed-input fallback never fabricates lone surrogates, so the slice-split case the amended spec text names is the only reachable producer; the spec's general invariant sentence ('A value must never end in an unpaired surrogate') covers the code's behavior.
